result.rule: When the description says that a group of activities may be carried out in parallel, starting from one point and leading to a later step that needs all of them finished: Open the group of parallel activities with a parallel gateway split placed after the point where they may start, give each activity its own outgoing branch from that split, and close the branches with a parallel gateway join before the later step. Do not sequence the activities one after another, and do not add decision conditions to these branches.

When the description joins two activities with 'and' (for example, one party performs both actions for the same case) and gives no stated order between them, so both must be completed before the flow continues: Model the two activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway split before them and a parallel gateway join after them, so the next step starts only when both branches have completed. Do not model them as a sequence with an arbitrary order, and do not model them as alternatives.

When the description states that one actor conducts two named activities joined by 'and' (for example 'X and Y') before a following activity: Model each named activity as its own task, not as one combined task. If both activities must be completed before the following activity, place them on parallel branches between a parallel split gateway and a parallel join gateway, then connect the join to the following activity.

When the description states that several follow-up actions after one activity are carried out in parallel (at the same time), and none of these follow-up actions depends on a condition: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one unconditional outgoing branch per follow-up action, with no decision conditions on those branches. Join the branches with a parallel gateway before any shared continuation, so the continuation waits for all of them.
